entries.title: Protests in Ukraine's cities against Zelensky's removal of defence minister
entries.snippet: Ukraine's president has not explained Mykhailo Fedorov's dismissal, which is causing great upset among civil society and the military.

entries.title: Iran targets military bases as US launches wave of strikes
entries.snippet: Explosions were heard across Iran overnight, shortly after neighbouring Gulf states began to report attacks.

entries.title: More than 800 Canadian wildfires burning as air quality alerts extend to US
entries.snippet: The air quality in large parts of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by authorities.

entries.title: Argentina face action over Falklands banner
entries.snippet: Argentina face the prospect of disciplinary action from Fifa after their players celebrate the World Cup semi-final win against England with a banner in support of their country's claims to the Falkland Islands.

entries.title: Volunteer firefighter suspected of starting devastating France forest fire
entries.snippet: President Macron said there would be no leniency for arsonists, as France - along with much of Europe - deals with a series of unusual heatwaves.

entries.title: 'Moment of joy' as Uganda discharges last Ebola patient
entries.snippet: Most of the recent cases were among travellers from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

entries.title: Families of 43 victims await verdict in Genoa bridge disaster
entries.snippet: A large section of the giant Morandi motorway bridge crumbled and collapsed on to the railway tracks below.

entries.title: Eleven people die in fire at Algerian children's care home
entries.snippet: Along with the fatalities, 19 people suffered injuries, the authorities say.

entries.title: New monkey species with orange lips found 'hiding' in DR Congo forest
entries.snippet: Scientists describe "amazing feeling" to look into the face of an animal that so few people knew existed.

entries.title: Fraud crackdown on Ghana ID cards makes digital checks compulsory - photocopies banned
entries.snippet: Companies are now required to verify a person's identity electronically to curb theft and forgery.

entries.title: Chip giant TSMC pledges another $100bn to expand US production
entries.snippet: The company says it will create "high-tech, high-paying jobs", and raises its total commitment to the US to $265bn.

entries.title: Actor Sam Neill died from pneumonia, agent confirms
entries.snippet: Neill died in Sydney on Monday, with his family saying his death was 'sudden and unexpected'.

entries.title: US military to start screening for testosterone deficiency, Hegseth says
entries.snippet: Hegseth says he is authorising hormone screening to ensure US troops "operate at your absolute best".

entries.title: More people around the world now favour China over the US, Pew study suggests
entries.snippet: There is more confidence in Xi Jinping than Donald Trump, the US think tank's survey indicates.

entries.title: Moment US Navy jet stuns packed Florida beach with low flypast
entries.snippet: A US Navy Blue Angels jet sent some beach items up in the air as it flew at a low altitude over a crowd in Pensacola Beach, Florida.

entries.title: Pakistan resisting UK attempts to deport grooming gang leader
entries.snippet: The government of Pakistan says it has "no connection whatsoever" with the case of Shabir Ahmed.

entries.title: Blanche apologises on Capitol Hill for Epstein files 'mistakes'
entries.snippet: Blanche faces a bipartisan grilling as he seeks to assume the role of US attorney general permanently.

entries.title: French MPs approve assisted dying law with strict rules after years of argument
entries.snippet: The bill would allow assisted dying for terminally ill adults who meet strict criteria.

entries.title: Russian attacks kill 14 as Ukraine hits Black Sea oil tankers
entries.snippet: Civilian casualties are reported in a number of Ukrainian regions, while Kyiv hits 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea.

entries.title: Special police team to investigate killing of an anti-migrant leader in South Africa
entries.snippet: The March and March provincial leader died of his injuries in hospital several days after being shot.

entries.title: Trump wants to fence off the park closest to the White House, a popular protest spot
entries.snippet: The Trump administration wants to install permanent fencing around Lafayette Park, directly outside the White House. It's long been a popular spot for protesters, who worry barriers will change that.

entries.title: Zelenskyy fires Ukraine's tech-savvy defense minister in government reshuffle
entries.snippet: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has fired the country's popular defense minister, who pushed for innovation in the battlefield through the use of drones and turned the tables on Russia.

entries.title: The political risks from war in Iran. And, ICE's use of force is rising, report finds
entries.snippet: The political implications the war in Iran is having on the GOP. And, a new report has found that ICE officers' use of force is not rare since President Trump took office for his second term.

entries.title: Oil companies are making billions. In the U.S., calls to tax their windfall are growing
entries.snippet: Higher oil prices since the Iran war began mean many oil companies have brought in excess profits. Some U.S. lawmakers want to tax those windfall profits and give the money to lower-income Americans.

entries.title: DHS pledged body cams for all immigration agents. Months later, that hasn't happened
entries.snippet: In recent days, federal immigration agents fatally shot two immigrant fathers. None of the federal officers involved were wearing body cameras, the agency said.

entries.title: Bike lanes and speed cameras disappear from the DOT's list of proven safety measures
entries.snippet: The Federal Highway Administration quietly stripped bike lanes and other safety recommendations from a key list of best practices. Critics say those measures are proven to cut crashes and save lives.

entries.title: TrumpRx promised a supermarket for cheaper drugs but delivered a boutique
entries.snippet: President Trump said TrumpRx is the biggest thing to happen in healthcare in decades. But an NPR analysis finds drugmakers are only offering deals on a few of their medicines.

entries.title: No Asian team managed to go far this World Cup (again). What's holding them back?
entries.snippet: For the sixth World Cup in a row, no team from the Asian Football Confederation made it past the first knockout round, winning only three games out of 29. Asian teams are competitive — up to a point.

entries.title: The use of force has become a 'default tool' for ICE officers, a new report finds
entries.snippet: An ACLU report looks at the widespread use of force in immigration enforcement in the first year of President Trump's return to office. Recent fatal shootings in Texas and Maine have brought renewed scrutiny to the agency's tactics.

entries.title: 'Gossip' had godly origins. Here's how it gained its sinful reputation
entries.snippet: We've all engaged in a little 'gossip.' But did you know its origins were tied to family and friendship?

entries.title: What Blanche said about Trump, Epstein files during confirmation hearing for attorney general
entries.snippet: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche tried to assert his independence from President Donald Trump during his confirmation hearing Wednesday before the Senate Judiciary Committee.

entries.title: Senators question Blanche on Trump loyalty, Jan. 6 cases and Epstein files
entries.snippet: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche appeared before the Senate Judiciary Committee for testimony on his nomination to serve permanently in the role. Blanche faced questions about his record as President Trump's personal lawyer, the fate of a proposed settlement fund for people w

entries.title: Trump's intelligence nominee refuses to say who won 2020 election
entries.snippet: Jay Clayton appeared before the Senate Intelligence Committee for his confirmation hearing to become director of national intelligence. The job is largely focused on foreign threats and national security, but much of the hearing focused instead on the recent past. Nick Schifrin r

entries.title: News Wrap: Trump ends pause on ICE traffic stops
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Wednesday, President Trump overturned the temporary pause on ICE traffic stops that was issued after two deadly shootings within a week, the U.S. launched multiple waves of new strikes against Iran, and heavy smoke from several wildfires burning in Canada and Min

entries.title: Subpoenas over New York Times report on Air Force One raise press freedom concerns
entries.snippet: Several New York Times reporters were subpoenaed to appear before a federal grand jury after the paper published stories raising security concerns about the new Air Force One. White House correspondent Liz Landers discusses questions the case is raising about freedom of the press

entries.title: Police say Flock cameras help solve crimes, but critics call them an invasion of privacy
entries.snippet: Law enforcement agencies in the U.S. use AI-powered cameras to scan billions of vehicles each month, often without drivers ever realizing. Supporters say the technology is a tool for solving crimes. But critics warn it's creating a nationwide surveillance network, raising urgent

entries.title: What to know about the latest push to make daylight saving time permanent
entries.snippet: Congress took its biggest step yet toward ending the twice-yearly changing of the clocks. The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make daylight saving time permanent nationwide. The bipartisan bill now heads to the Senate, where a similar effort stalled several

entries.title: 'Post-literate age': Why fewer Americans are reading for pleasure
entries.snippet: In recent years, there has been attention and worries about how reading has changed among kids. Those concerns include the nature of what kids are reading and how many fewer books are part of their education diet. A new cover story in The Atlantic is casting a broader spotlight,

entries.title: National Youth Poet Laureate Daniel Umemezie on using his words to bridge worlds
entries.snippet: For a decade, the National Youth Poet Laureate program has honored some of the country's top young writers who are using their work to inspire social change. Fred de Sam Lazaro recently sat down with the 2026-2027 laureate in his hometown of Cedar Falls, Iowa. It's part of our ar

entries.title: Federal government replaces slavery exhibition at Washington's home in Philadelphia
entries.snippet: "Overnight, under the cover of darkness, the federal government removed panels at the President's House that told a thorough history of Philadelphia," Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle L. Parker said.

entries.title: Starmer says his political journey is over at his last question session as UK leader
entries.snippet: Starmer, who leaves office next week, bid farewell to the boisterous weekly Prime Minister's Questions sessions where he has traded barbs with opposition politicians and defended his government's record.

entries.title: U.S. Mint produces a $1 coin bearing Trump's face to help celebrate America's 250th birthday
entries.snippet: The final design for the commemorative coin, being released in the fall, was approved earlier this year by the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were appointed by Trump.

entries.title: Trump administration 'screwed up' Epstein files communication, Vance says
entries.snippet: During a lengthy podcast interview with Joe Rogan released Wednesday, Vice President JD Vance pointed largely to former Attorney General Pam Bondi, who infamously stated that an alleged "client list" of Epstein's was "sitting on my desk right now."

entries.title: Biden will publish 'Promise Me, America' memoir after the November midterm elections
entries.snippet: The timing of the book — two weeks after midterm elections in which Democrats seek to regain control of Congress — could raise concerns within Biden's party by putting him back into the spotlight.

entries.title: Trump endorses 'Pillow Man' Mike Lindell for Minnesota governor
entries.snippet: Trump praised Lindell as "one of America's greatest and most hard working Patriots" and gave formal backing to a fellow election denier a day before the Republican president delivers a national address he says will focus on election security.

entries.title: Hegseth announces new policy to test troops for low testosterone and offer them hormone replacement therapy
entries.snippet: Many influencers and proponents of Robert F. Kennedy's "Make America Healthy Again" movement tout testosterone as a way to look younger, build muscle and stay mentally sharp — although those uses aren't accepted by most medical experts.

entries.title: Report: Detainees at ICE facility in Texas report frequent beatings and other human rights abuses
entries.snippet: The 84-page report issued jointly Wednesday by Human Rights Watch and the American Civil Liberties Union says men and women held at Camp East Montana, located at the U.S. Army's Fort Bliss in El Paso, recounted being denied necessary medical care, forced to live in filthy conditi

entries.title: Heavy smoke from wildfires blankets the Northeast and Mideast, prompting evacuations
entries.snippet: More than 100 wildfires are burning in Canada and winds are carrying the smoke southeast.

entries.title: WATCH: Erica Schwartz testifies in confirmation hearing for CDC director
entries.snippet: Schwartz told the Senate health committee she "will never betray the science" and pledged to use "radical transparency" in a bid to rebuild public trust in the agency. But several senators questioned how she might handle pressure from Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who h

entries.title: WATCH: Blanche defends his handling of Epstein files
entries.snippet: The nominee for attorney general acknowledged that his department made redaction mistakes and said dozens of lawyers were on call to quickly correct the errors.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Why America's hospitals keep looking to India for nurses
entries.snippet: Thousands of Indian nurses aspire to work in the US, navigating yearslong visa backlogs to fill a growing healthcare workforce shortage.

entries.title: Germany may make it illegal to deny Israel's right to exist
entries.snippet: Germany's upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat, has introduced a bill seeking to ban the questioning of Israel's right to exist. It is now up to the lower house to decide whether to turn it into law.

entries.title: The EU climate policy the world copied is under fire — what's at stake?
entries.snippet: The emissions trading system became a global blueprint for pricing carbon and cutting CO2. Now industry groups are pushing back against tougher climate rules. How effective is the scheme and where does it fall short?

entries.title: What's behind the Iran regime's 'revenge propaganda'?
entries.snippet: Calls for revenge over the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei are growing louder in Iran. Through increasingly harsh rhetoric, the leadership is seeking to mobilize supporters at home while warning opponents abroad.

entries.title: US slaps 25% tariffs on Brazil with election looming
entries.snippet: The US will impose a 25% tariff on most imports from Brazil starting later this month. It's the first action in the Trump administration's new tariff strategy, after the Supreme Court struck down its prior impositions.

entries.title: Ukraine lawmakers approve Koretskyi as new PM amid protests
entries.snippet: It is President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's second Cabinet shakeup in a year. He faces criticism for dismissing reformist Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Germany news: Gender switch neo-Nazi sent to men's prison
entries.snippet: Neo-Nazi Marla Svenja Liebich has been transferred to a men's prison after extradition back to Germany, despite being legally registered as a woman. DW has more.

entries.title: UK calls for FIFA investigation over Argentina banner
entries.snippet: Following their 2-1 World Cup semifinal victory over England, Argentine players held up a banner claiming the Falkland Islands belong to Argentina. Political messages are banned under FIFA rules.

entries.title: India news: Murders following romantic rejections increase
entries.snippet: The stabbing of a Bengaluru student after she reportedly turned down a marriage proposal is among a string of recent murders across India that involve violence following romantic rejections. DW has more.

entries.title: Iran threatens regional strikes as US intensifies attacks
entries.snippet: Iran has struck sites in Jordan and Gulf states after the US military widened its set of Iranian targets, including in the north of the country. DW has more.

entries.title: AI: Why Europe is falling behind, and how it can catch up
entries.snippet: Europe trails the US and China in artificial intelligence. Economist and Nobel laureate Philippe Aghion says better research funding, venture capital and AI innovation can help it catch up.

entries.title: Will gold prices extend their record-breaking run?
entries.snippet: Predictions suggest the price of the precious metal will keep hitting new record highs as investors seek a safe bet in turbulent times. Some forecasts say prices could double within five years.

entries.title: East-West border death zone now Germany's biodiversity oasis
entries.snippet: Many endangered species now live in the area that once formed the border between East and West Germany. Environment Minister Carsten Schneider recently visited the "Green Belt," and DW went along for the ride.

entries.title: Could Russia be about to lose its grip on chess leadership?
entries.snippet: Russians have long pulled the strings when it comes to the governing body of international chess. But now two Germans are vying for FIDE's top job.

entries.title: Myanmar: More than 500 feared dead in capsized refugee boats, UN says
entries.snippet: The UN has reported that two vessels carrying Rohingya refugees set off in hazardous conditions and are believed to have capsized. In recent years, thousands of Rohingya have attempted dangerous sea crossings.

entries.title: Alcatraz boat capsizing in San Francisco leaves 4 dead
entries.snippet: A three-deck pontoon vessel sank off the famous prison island, which is now a tourist destination. Three people who were missing are presumed dead after a search-and-rescue operation was called off.

entries.title: Hong Kong police raid two bookstores, arrest five people
entries.snippet: Five booksellers have been arrested in Hong Kong over the sale of allegedly "seditious" publications. Two bookstores have become the latest target in a continued crackdown on independent bookshops

entries.title: Trump administration replaces Philadelphia slavery memorial
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has replaced panels at a Philadelphia memorial about people enslaved by George Washington. Critics argue that the new exhibit presents a sanitized view of US history.

entries.title: France's parliament passes assisted dying law
entries.snippet: The lower house of France's parliament adopted bill for assisted dying. But the the government bypassed the right-wing dominated Senate and the law will instead go to the highest constitutional court for final approval.
